title: Property B Upper Bounds: Explicit Non-2-Colorable Hypergraphs Bracket m(k)
description: Answers (the explicit, elementary part of) the first-moment entry's open question OQ-01: bracket m(k) — the minimum number of edges in a non-2-colorable k-uniform hypergraph — from above. Two explicit witnesses are formalized. (1) General, all k: the complete k-uniform hypergraph on 2k−1 vertices is not 2-colorable, because any 2-coloring of 2k−1 vertices has a color class of size ≥ k whose k-subsets are monochromatic edges; this gives m(k) ≤ C(2k−1, k). (2) Sharp at k=3: the Fano plane PG(2,2) — 7 lines on 7 points — is not 2-colorable (verified by kernel `decide` over all 2^7 colorings, no native_decide), giving m(3) ≤ 7 < C(5,3) = 10. Combined with the parent's first-moment lower bound m(k) ≥ 2^(k-1) this yields, e.g., 4 ≤ m(3) ≤ 7. HONEST SCOPE: C(2k−1,k) ≈ 4^k/√(πk) is exponentially weaker than the Erdős–Lovász m(k) = O(k²·2^k); these are unconditional explicit witnesses, not the optimal probabilistic construction. Verified, 0 axioms, 0 sorries, no native_decide.

mathlibDependencies.description: n ≤ #s → ∃ t ⊆ s, #t = n. Extracts a k-element subset from a color class of size ≥ k; that subset is the monochromatic edge witnessing non-2-colorability of the complete hypergraph.
(s.filter p).card + (s.filter (¬p)).card = s.card. Splits the 2k−1 vertices into the c=true and c=false color classes, whose sizes sum to 2k−1, forcing one class to have ≥ k vertices (pigeonhole).
#(s.powersetCard n) = (#s).choose n. Counts the edges of the complete k-uniform hypergraph (all k-subsets of a (2k−1)-set) as C(2k−1, k).
t ∈ s.powersetCard n ↔ t ⊆ s ∧ #t = n. Certifies that the extracted k-subset is an edge of the complete hypergraph and that the hypergraph is k-uniform.

originalContributions: completeHypergraph_notTwoColorable: a fully general, elementary, 0-axiom proof that the complete k-uniform hypergraph on 2k−1 vertices admits no proper 2-coloring — pigeonhole on the two color classes (one has ≥ k vertices, hence a monochromatic k-edge) — yielding the explicit upper bound m(k) ≤ C(2k−1, k) that brackets the parent entry's first-moment lower bound m(k) ≥ 2^(k-1)

fano_notTwoColorable: a 0-axiom verification (kernel `decide` over all 2^7 = 128 colorings, NOT native_decide) that the Fano plane PG(2,2) — the seven lines {0,1,2},{0,3,4},{0,5,6},{1,3,5},{1,4,6},{2,3,6},{2,4,5} — is not 2-colorable, giving the sharp bound m(3) ≤ 7

exists_notTwoColorable_le_choose / exists_notTwoColorable_three: existence-form statements packaging each construction as a k-uniform, non-2-colorable hypergraph of the stated edge count, the precise shape needed to read off an upper bound on m(k)
fano_beats_general: the explicit comparison 7 < C(5,3) = 10 showing the Fano construction strictly improves the general complete-hypergraph bound at k = 3 (and is in fact the extremal value m(3) = 7)

overview.historicalContext: Erdős (1963) gave the first nontrivial lower bound m(k) ≥ 2^(k-1) on the minimum number of edges of a non-2-colorable (no Property B) k-uniform hypergraph, via the first moment method (formalized in the parent entry). The matching upper side asks for SMALL non-2-colorable hypergraphs. The elementary universal construction is the complete k-uniform hypergraph on 2k−1 vertices: pigeonhole forces a monochromatic edge under any 2-coloring, so m(k) ≤ C(2k−1, k). For k = 3 the projective plane PG(2,2) (the Fano plane, 7 points, 7 lines) is non-2-colorable and is the extremal example, m(3) = 7. The true growth rate sits in the narrow window 2^(k-1) ≤ m(k) ≤ O(k²·2^k), the upper bound being the Erdős–Lovász (1973) probabilistic construction; the explicit bounds here are weaker but unconditional and fully verified.
overview.problemStatement: Let $m(k)$ be the least number of edges in a $k$-uniform hypergraph with no proper 2-coloring (no Property B). Exhibit explicit non-2-colorable $k$-uniform hypergraphs to bound $m(k)$ from above: (i) the complete $k$-uniform hypergraph on $2k-1$ vertices gives $m(k) \le \binom{2k-1}{k}$; (ii) the Fano plane gives the sharp $m(3) \le 7$. With Erdős' lower bound $m(k) \ge 2^{k-1}$ this brackets $m(k)$, e.g. $4 \le m(3) \le 7$.
overview.text: A k-uniform hypergraph fails to be 2-colorable when every 2-coloring leaves some edge monochromatic. To bound m(k) from above we only need ONE small such hypergraph. The complete hypergraph on 2k−1 vertices works for every k by sheer pigeonhole; for k = 3 the Fano plane does much better, hitting the exact extremal value 7.
overview.proofStrategy:
Reuse the parent's notions: an edge is a Finset of vertices, Mono e c means all of e is one color, and NotTwoColorable E means ∀ c, ∃ e ∈ E, Mono e c.

1. **General bound (completeHypergraph_notTwoColorable).** Take V = Fin (2k−1) and E = all k-subsets (univ.powersetCard k). Given a coloring c, the true-class {x | c x = true} and false-class {x | c x = false} partition V (filter_card_add_filter_neg_card_eq_card), so their sizes sum to 2k−1; by omega one class has size ≥ k. Extract a k-subset S of that class (exists_subset_card_eq); S is an edge (mem_powersetCard) and is monochromatic. Edge count is C(2k−1, k) (card_powersetCard). Hence m(k) ≤ C(2k−1, k).

2. **Sharp k=3 (fano_notTwoColorable).** Encode the seven Fano lines as explicit Finsets of Fin 7. NotTwoColorable unfolds to a decidable proposition over the finite type Fin 7 → Bool (128 colorings), discharged by kernel `decide` (with maxRecDepth raised) — no native_decide, so axiom-free. Edge count 7 and 3-uniformity are likewise `decide`d. Hence m(3) ≤ 7, and 7 < C(5,3) = 10 (fano_beats_general).

3. **Bracket.** Combined with the parent's m(k) ≥ 2^(k-1): 2^(k-1) ≤ m(k) ≤ C(2k−1, k) for all k, and the sharp 4 ≤ m(3) ≤ 7.
keyInsights: **An upper bound on m(k) needs just one witness.** Unlike the lower bound (a universal statement over all small hypergraphs), bounding m(k) from above only requires exhibiting a single non-2-colorable k-uniform hypergraph, so the proofs are constructions plus a non-colorability certificate

**Pigeonhole gives the universal bound for free.** On 2k−1 vertices some color class has ≥ k vertices; in the COMPLETE hypergraph any k of them form an edge, so the bound C(2k−1, k) requires no probabilistic argument at all

**The Fano plane is the sharp k=3 example.** Its non-2-colorability is a genuinely finite fact verifiable by kernel `decide` over 128 colorings; it gives m(3) ≤ 7, strictly better than the general C(5,3) = 10, and matches the known extremal value m(3) = 7

**`decide` keeps it axiom-free.** Using kernel reduction rather than native_decide means the Fano certificate adds no Lean.ofReduceBool axiom — the whole file rests only on propext/Classical.choice/Quot.sound
**Honest gap to Erdős–Lovász.** C(2k−1,k) ≈ 4^k/√(πk) is exponentially larger than the optimal O(k²·2^k); this entry brackets m(k) explicitly but does not close the window

sections.title: Module Header and Scope
sections.summary: Frames the upper-bound companion to the first-moment lower bound m(k) ≥ 2^(k-1): two explicit non-2-colorable witnesses (complete hypergraph on 2k−1 vertices, and the Fano plane at k=3), with an honest note that C(2k-1,k) is exponentially weaker than the Erdős–Lovász O(k²·2^k).

sections.title: Definitions: Mono and NotTwoColorable
sections.summary: Reintroduces Mono e c (∃ b, ∀ x ∈ e, c x = b) with its Decidable instance, matching the parent entry, and defines NotTwoColorable E := ∀ c : V → Bool, ∃ e ∈ E, Mono e c as the negation of Property B.

sections.title: General Bound m(k) ≤ C(2k-1, k) via the Complete Hypergraph
sections.summary: completeHypergraph k = univ.powersetCard k on Fin (2k−1). completeHypergraph_uniform/_card give k-uniformity and edge count C(2k−1,k). completeHypergraph_notTwoColorable: the color classes partition 2k−1 vertices (filter_card_add_filter_neg_card_eq_card), one has size ≥ k (omega), and a k-subset of it (exists_subset_card_eq) is a monochromatic edge. exists_notTwoColorable_le_choose packages this as m(k) ≤ C(2k−1, k).

sections.title: Sharp Bound m(3) ≤ 7 via the Fano Plane
sections.summary: fanoLines: the 7 lines of PG(2,2) on Fin 7. fano_uniform (3-uniform) and fano_card (7 edges) by `decide`. fano_notTwoColorable: NotTwoColorable unfolds to a decidable statement over Fin 7 → Bool and is discharged by kernel `decide` over all 128 colorings (no native_decide). exists_notTwoColorable_three packages m(3) ≤ 7; fano_beats_general records 7 < C(5,3) = 10.

conclusion.summary: Explicit, fully verified non-2-colorable k-uniform hypergraphs bound the Property B threshold m(k) from above: the complete hypergraph on 2k−1 vertices gives m(k) ≤ C(2k−1, k) for all k by pigeonhole, and the Fano plane gives the sharp m(3) ≤ 7 by kernel `decide` over all 128 colorings. Together with the parent's first-moment lower bound m(k) ≥ 2^(k-1) this brackets m(k), e.g. 4 ≤ m(3) ≤ 7. 0 axioms, 0 sorries, no native_decide.
conclusion.implications: This entry answers the explicit/elementary part of the parent's OQ-01 (bracket m(k) from above) and completes a two-sided bound for the same m(k) defined there. The Fano result demonstrates that the extremal small case is decidable axiom-free, and the general pigeonhole bound provides a reusable template for upper-bounding 2-colorability thresholds via complete hypergraphs.
openQuestions: Formalize the Erdős–Lovász probabilistic upper bound m(k) = O(k²·2^k), closing the gap between the explicit C(2k−1, k) here and the parent's 2^(k-1) lower bound.
Prove the matching lower bound m(3) ≥ 7 (every 3-uniform hypergraph with ≤ 6 edges is 2-colorable), establishing the exact value m(3) = 7 with the Fano plane as the unique extremal example.
